NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior SRE and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering, Terraform, platform design and operation, and leading technical work across product and platform teams. Builds reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure that help teams deploy and operate services effectively.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment design and operation
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane
Platforms and deployment: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and systems: Go, Python, Bash, Linux, Puppet
Testing: k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS) | Manchester / remote
Apr 2022 – Present
- Tech lead for a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams; reduced the time for a new service to reach production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Led the move from cluster-autoscaler managed node groups to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
- Introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services, with error-budget policy agreed with product leadership. Reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Serve in the incident commander rotation and established incident and post-mortem processes.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | Leeds
Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure (EC2, ECS and later EKS) for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed infrastructure as code in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for plan and apply through pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Ran k6 load tests and launch-day capacity planning, including tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players; identified and helped resolve a connection-pool limit before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting | Sheffield
Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes preview namespace cleanup operator | Open source side project | 2024
- Built a small Go Kubernetes controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; received approximately 120 GitHub stars.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

ADDITIONAL
Speaker, UK DevOps meetup (2024): “SLOs that product managers care about”
Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend engineering into SRE
Languages: English (native), Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear senior-level scope, measurable outcomes, relevant certifications, and credible technical ownership. The strongest evidence includes the internal developer platform adopted by all 14 product teams, the 38% EC2 cost reduction, reduced on-call pages, large-scale EKS operation, and capacity testing for 300,000 concurrent players. The document is professional and concise. Its main limitation is not general CV quality but role-specific evidence: networking/security experience and the exact system-design language required by the advert are not sufficiently explicit. The selected project and speaking/mentoring content add useful evidence of technical depth and communication.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, readable text, standard chronological experience, explicit technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or headers/footers. Keyword coverage is strong for AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, observability, Linux, and technical leadership. AI screening probability is high for the AWS/platform/SRE aspects of the role, but only moderate for the complete advert because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, networking, practical security, and explicit systems architecture/system design terminology are absent. These are genuine evidence gaps or weakly evidenced areas, not terms that should be added without supporting experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with hands-on AWS infrastructure engineering, cloud platform design and operation, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, reliability, observability, Linux, technical leadership, analytical problem solving, and developer enablement. It also reflects Corvale's ownership-oriented and engineering-led culture through platform ownership, self-service infrastructure, incident leadership, mentoring, and collaboration with product leadership. The candidate's Go/Python platform work provides relevant backend-adjacent experience. The main job-alignment gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, explicit network design, practical security experience, and IoT/automotive/remote-device integration. The CV also does not demonstrate JVM experience, although JVM is only a preference within the nice-to-have requirement.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the system-design alignment more explicit using only the experience already described. Change the sentence beginning “Experienced in hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering” to: “Experienced in hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment design and operation, platform architecture, Terraform, and leading technical work across product and platform teams.”

2. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, revise the internal developer platform bullet so it explicitly contains the advert's system-design terminology while remaining truthful. For example: “Designed and built an internal developer platform and its self-service architecture, using Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3.”

3. In the same Tallybrook section, make stakeholder leadership more explicit by revising the SLO bullet to: “Introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services; agreed the error-budget policy with product leadership and reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.” This preserves the existing evidence while directly demonstrating stakeholder alignment.

4. In the Core Skills section, change “cloud environment design and operation” to “AWS cloud environment design and operation” and change “SLOs and error budgets” to “SLOs, error budgets and reliability policy.” This improves exact keyword matching without adding unsupported technology or experience.

5. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, automotive integration, or security tools to the CV unless the candidate can substantiate that experience. The supplied candidate information does not currently support those claims.
